action: Patients: the emergency room is reported to be taking patients again; check with the hospital about any postponed appointments. Other hospitals should confirm they can run emergency care without IT and that backups are kept offline.
exec: An attack on hospital IT interrupted emergency care, showing the patient-safety stakes of IT resilience.
impact: Emergency room unavailable from 15 November; Freie Presse reported on 17 November that it is taking patients again.
plain: A cyberattack on a district hospital in Greiz, Germany, discovered on November 15, closed its emergency room. By November 17 it was reported to be taking patients again. Whether data was taken is not settled.
summary: The Greiz district says a cyberattack on its hospital was discovered on Sunday, November 15, and the emergency room was unavailable. Kommunal.de reports the district describes it as an extortion attempt; whether data was taken is not publicly settled and the clinic gives no information on patient data. Freie Presse reported on November 17 that the emergency room is taking patients again.
title: Cyberattack closes emergency room at Greiz-Ronneburg hospital in Germany

validation.note: Read Landkreis Greiz (15 Nov, attack found ~9:00, ER unavailable), kommunal.de (17 Nov, extortion attempt per district, data unsettled), Freie Presse (17 Nov, ER taking patients), kma-online (16 Nov), pasqualepillitteri.it (loads now; police say unauthorized access, no data theft confirmed). Removed unsupported ransomware tag and "roughly two days".
